articles.title: Documenting essential household records
articles.summary: Create a portable reference to critical household information.
body: List identification, insurance, property, financial, and emergency contact records needed during displacement.
Keep originals secured; prepare copies only when lawful and appropriate.
Store digital copies in an encrypted location and protect access credentials separately.
Include policy numbers and provider contact details without recording passwords in the document.
Maintain a paper contact sheet in a sealed, water resistant sleeve.
Identify an authorized person who can retrieve records if the primary custodian is unavailable.
Review after moves, policy renewals, and household changes.
Do not include personal record copies in shared or public article modules.

articles.title: Neighborhood welfare check planning
articles.summary: Organize voluntary checks after a disruption without exposing volunteers to hazards.
body: Identify neighbors who have opted in to being contacted and record preferred communication methods privately.
Establish a check sequence that begins with phone or radio before any physical visit.
Assign pairs when conditions permit and tell a coordinator where each pair is going.
Avoid entering damaged buildings, floodwater, downed wire areas, or locations restricted by responders.
Ask whether immediate assistance or emergency services are needed; do not diagnose conditions.
Record contact time, response, urgent needs, and any referral using minimal personal information.
Escalate life threatening situations to emergency services when available.
Close the loop by confirming that requested assistance was delivered or handed off.

articles.title: Plain language radio message format
articles.summary: Use a repeatable structure to pass accurate short radio messages.
body: Identify the intended recipient and your station according to the rules of the radio service.
State whether the message is emergency, priority, or routine without misusing distress calls.
Give the location with a recognizable reference and repeat coordinates when accuracy matters.
Describe the observed situation, time of observation, and whether the information is firsthand.
State the requested action and any relevant deadline.
Read back critical numbers, addresses, and instructions for confirmation.
Log the time, sender, recipient, and disposition of the message.
Follow applicable licensing, frequency, and emergency traffic procedures.

articles.title: Radio battery rotation and charging log
articles.summary: Keep portable radios available during prolonged power interruptions.
body: Inventory each radio and battery by a unique local label.
Record battery chemistry and use only a charger intended for that pack.
Check for swelling, leaks, heat damage, and damaged contacts; isolate suspect packs safely.
Set a routine to check charge state without repeatedly deep discharging batteries.
Prioritize charging for radios assigned to active duty and emergency monitoring.
Keep spare packs cool and dry within manufacturer storage limits.
Log charging start, finish, observed faults, and next inspection date.
Do not charge damaged batteries or leave improvised charging systems unattended.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Portable power bank inventory
articles.summary: Track available stored energy and prioritize essential devices.
body: List each power bank by capacity, connector type, and supported output ratings.
Record which critical devices each bank can actually charge.
Test cables and adapters before an outage.
Label dedicated banks for communications, lighting, and accessibility equipment.
Recharge and inspect according to manufacturer instructions.
Keep lithium batteries away from excessive heat, water, and puncture hazards.
Track estimated remaining charge rather than assuming nameplate capacity equals usable energy.
Never use damaged, swollen, or overheating packs.

articles.title: Accessible evacuation communication cards
articles.summary: Prepare concise instructions that support communication and reunification.
body: Ask each person what information they want responders or helpers to know.
Include preferred name, communication method, and emergency contact details with consent.
Describe essential equipment or support needs in simple, actionable terms.
Use large readable print and symbols where useful.
Include a current date and an instruction to verify information when possible.
Keep one copy with the person and another with their designated caregiver where appropriate.
Protect privacy and avoid placing unnecessary medical details on publicly visible cards.
Practice using the card during a household evacuation drill.

articles.title: Post storm exterior inspection from a safe distance
articles.summary: Recognize hazards before approaching a damaged property.
body: Wait for official clearance and avoid traveling through restricted or flooded areas.
Observe the building from a safe location before approaching.
Look for sagging roofs, leaning walls, broken glass, hanging branches, and unstable debris.
Assume every downed wire is energized; keep away and report it to the utility or emergency services.
Do not enter standing water near electrical equipment.
If you smell gas or hear a leak, leave the area and contact the utility or emergency services from safety.
Photograph visible damage only when it can be done without approaching hazards.
Seek a qualified inspection before reentering a building with structural or electrical damage.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Clean water container labeling
articles.summary: Prevent confusion between potable, untreated, and utility water.
body: Choose food grade containers appropriate for drinking water.
Clean and sanitize containers using current public health guidance before filling.
Label each container clearly as drinking water, untreated water, or nonpotable utility water.
Add fill date and source to the label.
Keep caps and dispensing tools clean and avoid touching the inside of openings.
Store away from fuels, chemicals, direct sunlight, and extreme heat.
Use a separate scoop or spigot for untreated water to prevent cross contamination.
If water safety is uncertain, follow current local health authority treatment instructions before drinking.

articles.title: Handwashing station setup during water interruptions
articles.summary: Provide a dedicated handwashing location when normal plumbing is unavailable.
body: Choose a stable surface away from food preparation and drinking water storage.
Provide a clean water container with a controlled pour or spigot, soap, and a catch basin.
Label the station for handwashing and keep untreated water separate.
Arrange drainage or collection so wastewater does not pool or contaminate living areas.
Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, including between fingers and under nails.
Prioritize washing after toilet use, before food preparation, and after handling waste.
Empty wastewater into an approved disposal location according to local instructions.
Refill and clean the station routinely; avoid shared standing wash water.

articles.title: Refrigerator and freezer temperature log
articles.summary: Use measured temperatures to inform food safety decisions during outages.
body: Keep an appliance thermometer in the refrigerator and freezer before an outage.
Record the time power failed and keep doors closed as much as possible.
Log actual thermometer readings and times rather than estimating from how food feels.
A refrigerator should generally remain at or below 40°F and a freezer at 0°F or below during normal operation.
Follow USDA and FDA outage guidance when deciding whether perishable foods must be discarded.
Do not taste food to determine safety; appearance and odor alone are unreliable.
Discard food exposed to floodwater or other contamination.
When in doubt about safety, discard the item rather than risk illness.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Paper map annotation for evacuation routes
articles.summary: Prepare usable route references when electronic navigation is unavailable.
body: Obtain a current regional road map and identify the map edition or date.
Mark primary and alternate destinations with clear symbols.
Highlight routes while preserving printed road names and legends.
Mark bridges, low water crossings, and other known constraints without assuming they will remain passable.
Record official evacuation zone and shelter information separately so it can be updated.
Add fuel, rest, and accessibility stops as planning references, not guaranteed services.
Store the map in a protective sleeve with a pencil.
Use official closures and evacuation instructions over a preplanned route.

articles.title: Two minute household departure check
articles.summary: Use a short checklist before leaving during a time sensitive evacuation.
body: Follow immediate evacuation orders and do not delay departure to complete a checklist.
Account for people and essential mobility or medical support items.
Take keys, phones, necessary medications, and accessible emergency information if already at hand.
Check that required assistance for children, pets, and dependent adults is assigned.
Use the safest available exit and avoid elevators during fire emergencies.
Do not reenter to retrieve forgotten possessions.
Tell an out of area contact where the household is heading when safe.
Confirm arrival and update the contact if the destination changes.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Indoor shelter area selection
articles.summary: Choose a safer interior location for applicable severe weather hazards.
body: Identify the hazard first; tornado, hurricane, flood, fire, and chemical incidents require different shelter decisions.
For tornado warnings, use a small interior room on the lowest safe floor, away from windows.
Do not shelter in a basement when flooding is occurring or expected.
Keep an accessible route for all household members.
Move away from glass, large unsupported roof spans, and exterior doors when appropriate.
Store flashlights, sturdy footwear, and communication devices nearby.
Use official alerts for shelter instructions and evacuation orders.
Reassess if water enters, smoke develops, or the structure becomes unsafe.

articles.title: Volunteer assignment board
articles.summary: Track who is doing what without exposing sensitive information.
body: Create columns for task, location, assigned person, check in time, and status.
Use simple statuses such as pending, assigned, active, and complete.
Prioritize life safety tasks and route hazardous work to qualified responders.
Record task limitations, required equipment, and communication method.
Give each team a check in interval and an escalation contact.
Do not post medical details or private addresses on a publicly visible board.
Close tasks only after the receiving person confirms completion.
Archive completed assignments for the after action review.

articles.title: Offline document backup verification
articles.summary: Confirm that an emergency reference archive can actually be opened.
body: List the files and applications needed to read critical information.
Copy the archive to a second storage device using the operating system file manager.
Open a representative sample of documents from the backup device, not the original.
Check that file names and folder structures remain understandable offline.
Record the backup date and device label.
Keep a second copy in a separate safe location when practical.
Protect sensitive data using appropriate encryption and access controls.
Repeat the test after major updates and before storm season.

articles.title: Daily incident activity log
articles.summary: Capture decisions and observations in chronological order.
body: Start each page with the date, time zone, incident name, and recorder.
Use a consistent time format for all entries.
Record significant observations separately from assumptions or reports from others.
Include the source and time received for secondhand information.
Document decisions, assigned actions, and expected follow up.
Correct mistakes with a dated note rather than silently deleting history.
Keep private personal information to the minimum required.
Transfer or secure the log at shift change.

articles.title: Household check in during extended disruptions
articles.summary: Maintain clear expectations and identify emerging support needs.
body: Choose a predictable short check in time each day.
Ask each person about immediate needs, concerns, and available energy without requiring disclosure.
Explain known facts, uncertainties, and the next planned update.
Assign manageable tasks that match each person’s abilities and preferences.
Make space for rest, quiet, and private time.
Avoid spreading unverified rumors or alarming speculation.
Identify when professional medical or crisis support is needed and seek it when available.
Record practical follow up actions without documenting unnecessary personal disclosures.

articles.title: Vehicle readiness before evacuation season
articles.summary: Inspect basic supplies and service status before travel is urgent.
body: Review fuel or charge range and identify realistic refueling alternatives.
Check tire condition and pressure when tires are cold, using the vehicle placard.
Verify lights, wipers, windshield fluid, and mirrors.
Check service reminders and address safety critical defects with a qualified mechanic.
Keep registration, insurance, and roadside contact details accessible.
Load appropriate water, charging cables, first aid supplies, and a flashlight.
Plan for passengers, child restraints, accessibility needs, and pets.
Never run a vehicle engine in a garage or enclosed space.

articles.title: Carbon monoxide alarm inspection
articles.summary: Check that carbon monoxide warning devices are present and functioning.
body: Identify every installed carbon monoxide alarm and its manufacturer instructions.
Confirm placement and replacement dates according to applicable codes and manufacturer guidance.
Use the test button as directed; it does not verify sensor calibration.
Replace batteries or the entire alarm when indicated by the manufacturer.
Never use fuel burning generators, grills, or camp stoves indoors or in attached garages.
If an alarm sounds, move everyone to fresh air immediately and contact emergency services.
Do not reenter until responders or qualified personnel say it is safe.
Record inspection dates and replacement needs.

articles.title: Field clothing layer inventory
articles.summary: Match spare clothing to expected conditions and individual needs.
body: List expected temperature, rain, wind, and exposure duration for the operating area.
Choose a moisture managing base layer, insulating layer, and protective outer layer as conditions require.
Keep spare socks and dry clothing protected in a waterproof bag.
Check fit and mobility with equipment already worn.
Include gloves, head covering, and sun protection where appropriate.
Avoid relying on cotton clothing for insulation when wet in cold conditions.
Inspect items for damage and replace worn weather protection.
Reassess clothing requirements as forecasts and seasons change.
